methodological_rigor.justification: International multi-institutional pooled cohort (DFCI, MDACC, INCORPORATE, plus PELICAN phase II) addressing a rare disease (TN-IBC) where prospective data are scarce. The hybrid retrospective/prospective design combining three retrospective cohorts with one randomized phase II arm introduces heterogeneity in eligibility (ER/PR cutoffs 1% vs 10%), chemotherapy backbones (carboplatin in 84.8% of non-PELICAN vs 0% in PELICAN), and follow-up duration. Absence of a contemporaneous control arm and the authors' own acknowledgment that carboplatin's contribution cannot be dissected from pembrolizumab limit causal inference. Sample size justification is based on precision of a 95% CI rather than a formal hypothesis test.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Observational multicenter cohort; Oxford LoE 4 (cohort without contemporaneous control). TN-IBC was represented by only 17 patients (1.4%) in KEYNOTE-522, so this is the first dedicated TN-IBC analysis of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, with direct relevance to an aggressive, rare subtype where evidence is otherwise extrapolated. The 31.7% pCR rate (vs 18% historical control) is clinically informative despite the confounding carboplatin effect.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort for which STROBE is the applicable standard; STROBE is not explicitly cited in the text. The manuscript reports eligibility, cohort-level demographics (Table 1), outcome definitions, and limitations, but lacks some STROBE-recommended items such as handling of missing data and full description of how cohorts were merged across jurisdictions. Data availability is limited: no repository or supplementary data-sharing statement is visible in the normalized text, and cohort-level case report forms are not shared.

novelty_literature.justification: First multi-cohort assessment of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy specifically in non-metastatic TN-IBC, filling an evidence gap left by KEYNOTE-522 which enrolled only 17 IBC patients. The underlying regimen (pembrolizumab + carboplatin/taxane/anthracycline) is established standard of care; the contribution is applying it and measuring pCR in a previously under-represented population rather than a new biological or methodological discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Short, focused manuscript with a clear IMRaD structure. Tables 1 and 2 stratify by cohort, allowing transparent comparisons, and the Discussion explicitly acknowledges the carboplatin confounder and cross-study comparability issues. Figures are absent (only two tables), which is appropriate for the scope, though a forest plot of pCR rates across cohorts would have enhanced visual communication.

key_strengths: Addresses an underserved rare subtype (TN-IBC) with dedicated multi-institutional data where KEYNOTE-522 included only 17 IBC patients
Pooled international cohort (n=63) across DFCI, MDACC, INCORPORATE, and PELICAN trial
Transparent cohort-stratified reporting and candid discussion of confounders (carboplatin effect)
pCR rate (31.7%, 95% CI 20.6-44.7%) provides benchmark for future TN-IBC trials
key_concerns: No contemporaneous control arm; comparison to 18% historical pCR confounded by absence of carboplatin in that reference
Heterogeneous eligibility (ER/PR thresholds differ between DFCI/MDACC/INCORPORATE and PELICAN) and variable chemotherapy regimens
Small sample (n=63) and short median follow-up (1.4 years) limit survival inference
Lack of baseline cN status and post-neoadjuvant therapy data, acknowledged by authors
No data-sharing statement or individual patient data repository visible
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically relevant pooled analysis filling a specific evidence gap in TN-IBC but methodologically constrained by retrospective design, cohort heterogeneity, and confounding of pembrolizumab vs carboplatin effects; fits tier 3 with minor revisions to strengthen reporting transparency.
